newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican treasurer says Telmex funds accounted for.
newsitem.headline: Mexican treasurer says Telmex funds accounted for.

text.p: The Mexican federal treasurer said on Friday that $1.34 billion that was suspected missing after the privatization of Telefonos de Mexico had in fact always been accounted for.

"It appears very important to emphasise that the funds coming from the sale of the second tranche of Telmex in May 1992, have never been missing, nor have we ever lost control of the funds," Jonathan Davis told members of a commission of Congress looking at the public accounts.
Mexican lawmakers said earlier that $1.34 billion was missing from the 1990 privatization of the phone company.

The Mexican press denounced the missing cash in banner headlines and speculated that officials may have carried on a murky tradition in 1994 of stuffing pockets with public funds just before the president's six-year-term came to a close.
But the congressmen who pointed out the anomalies also said the money may have been misplaced due to accounting errors and could show up eventually as other audits were carried out.
Davis said that the federal government had given orders that the funds be credited to a special fund set up by Banco de Mexico.
"The funds were effectively received and Banco de Mexico proceeded to credit the dollar account that the federal treasury had open with the central bank," he said.
He said the funds had always been accounted for and were used to amortize the external debt.

"So the funds were always accounted for. We knew perfectly their dates of entry and destination. We have all the supporting documents, the accounts with Banco de Mexico and their respective receipts," Davis said.
